citation: docs/mip/0004-agent-messaging.md, sections 2 to 5 and 13, and its table of what council v1 got wrong
why: What the message service does is a function of its participants, their groups, the logs and cursors, and whose inbox still answers, so it is data: each case is a script of steps by named callers, and each step is answered with one line. A caller is a Claude session (`session`, whose inbox socket is /tmp/cc-socks/<session>.sock), a name given with --as (`as`), or neither, which is the human. `dies` makes a session's inbox stop answering. Groups number their entries from 1, and creating one logs `created` and the creator's join before anything else.

v1.why: MIP-4 section 15 holds that each failure of council v1 that policy or delivery answers is a named case here. Each row of its table is listed by the table's first column, with the case that answers it, or with where it is answered instead; the driver reads the table and fails when the two disagree.

a body never travels through a PTY (MIP-4, section 4): muster-cli's a_body_comes_whole_from_a_file_or_stdin, and claude_code_doorbell's brief read whole

cases.name: a newcomer's reading starts when it joins, and the log still holds what came before
cases.why: Council v1's CLI kept no cursor, so every post carried a hand-counted `--after N`. Each participant has a read cursor, which starts at its join: history from before is what `log` is for, and counting it as unread would refuse the newcomer's first post (MIP-4, section 4).

cases.name: a name must be one a command line and a log can carry
cases.why: Names appear in commands, notices and file names, so they are letters, digits, dot, underscore and hyphen (MIP-4, section 11 for why they must be unique).

cases.name: a group whose name differs from another's only in case is refused
cases.why: On a filesystem that ignores case, which is macOS's default, two such groups would share one log file and merge after a restart; a person would not tell them apart either (MIP-4, section 12).

cases.name: a group name is short enough to be a file name
cases.why: Each group's log is a file named after it, and a file name has at most 255 bytes (MIP-4, section 12).

cases.name: a post to so many that their group's name would be too long is refused
cases.why: A post to agents who share no group creates the group of exactly them, named after them; past the length a group name may be, the author has to make a group and name it (MIP-4, sections 2 and 12).

cases.name: a session cannot act as a live participant it is not
cases.why: join --name refuses the name of a live participant, and --as on any verb is held to the same rule: otherwise a mistyped --as moves that participant's inbox to the caller, and the real one is never woken again. A caller with no session of its own, such as a script, may act as it without moving anything (MIP-4, section 3).

cases.name: a session that takes over a name is woken, whatever the old one was told
cases.why: A wake went to the old session, which exited before reading; the session that comes back under its name has been woken for nothing yet (MIP-4, section 3, Coming back).

cases.name: the human's wait is answered by a post for the human
cases.why: Council v1's last agent waited forever on "Moderator", since `await` never released on the human. The human is a participant like any other: a person's script waiting on a message is a wait like any other, and the windows are told as well, since the person may not be the one running it (MIP-4, sections 10 and 13).

cases.why: Between tool calls its PostToolUse hook reads, and at the end of a turn its Stop hook waits, so typing into its pane would only repeat them. Hooks that have run in the last five minutes are running; after that the doorbell takes over, in case they stopped (MIP-4, sections 6 and 7).

cases.why: A turn that ends in an API error, or that a person stops with Esc, runs no Stop hook, so nothing fetches what the agent's hooks were counted on to fetch mid-turn. Going idle with no wait connected, it is rung for it, once, as an agent without hooks is (MIP-4, sections 5 and 6).

cases.why: Council v1 delivered only to an agent blocked in `await`, so one that had started working was unreachable until it looped back.
